spec.title: Tabletop bottle transfer A to B (300 g, 10 per minute)
spec.summary: A fixed tabletop arm with a parallel gripper picks up a closed 300 g plastic bottle (Ø0.07 m × 0.22 m) standing upright at point A. It carries it 0.6 m across a 0.75 m high table and sets it down upright at point B within ±5 mm. Target rate is 10 transfers per minute, so each cycle takes 6 s. The robot does not drive.
spec.frame: World frame: metres, z up, origin on the floor below the robot base. The table top is at z = 0.75. Markers sit at z on the table surface.

actions.description: Move from home to the approach pose 0.1 m above the bottle's grasp height at A, then descend.
Close the parallel gripper on the bottle body at about mid-height, then lift it 0.1 m clear of the table.
Carry the bottle upright across 0.6 m to the approach pose above B.
Lower the bottle onto the table at B within ±5 mm, open the gripper and retract.
Return to the ready pose for the next bottle.

spec.environment: Indoor, on a 0.75 m high table, clean and dry, room temperature.
spec.duty_cycle: Continuous: 10 cycles per minute (600 per hour), one shift per day.
spec.speed_target: 10 bottles per minute, a 6 s cycle.
spec.payload_description: A closed plastic bottle weighing 0.3 kg, a cylinder 0.07 m across and 0.22 m tall. It must stay upright from A to B. The gripper holds it from the side with two contacts at about mid-height.
assumptions: The robot is a fixed arm on the table top, centred between A and B 0.45 m in front of its base. A and B are 0.6 m apart along y.
Grip is a parallel gripper with friction pads (μ ≈ 0.4 on plastic), 2 contacts.
The bottle must stay upright for the whole move, and its position at A is known to about ±5 mm.
Cycle time is 6 s from the requested 10 per minute, and the timing of each step is an estimate.
Peak acceleration of the tool is limited to 3 m/s² so the liquid doesn't slosh and the bottle doesn't slip.
Approach and lift height is 0.1 m above the grasp point, with 0.05 m clearance.
The robot runs one shift per day.
spec.reference: No reference robot was given. Reach and payload come from the task: the arm needs about 0.55 m of reach and at least 1 kg of payload with margin.

robot.name: 4-axis tabletop bottle mover
robot.rationale: The task asks for a fixed arm on a table, and a serial arm can reach both A and B with the tool pointing down. Four axes are enough because the round bottle needs no tool roll, so no extra wrist joints are needed. A gantry would also handle the 0.6 m straight move, but it needs a frame over the table. A serial arm has its limits: the cycle-time targets ask for high TCP speed and acceleration, which puts heavy loads on the shoulder and elbow drives at nearly 1 m reach. Joint speeds and torques are left for the sizing code to set.
